name: Interactive Task and Concept Learning from Natural Language Instructions and GUI Demonstrations
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available for this review. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces PUMICE, an agent that learns mobile-app procedures and conditional concepts through natural-language conversation and GUI demonstrations, recursively resolving ambiguous instructions with users.

publication.title: Multimodal Web Navigation with Instruction-Finetuned Foundation Models

name: Multimodal Web Navigation with Instruction-Finetuned Foundation Models
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Trains WebGUM offline from demonstrations by jointly tuning an instruction-following language model and a vision encoder over webpage screenshots and HTML. The agent predicts browser actions and is evaluated on MiniWoB, WebShop, and Mind2Web.

name: Grounded Language Agent for Product Search via Intelligent Web Interactions
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces GLAINTEL, a Flan-T5-based product-search web agent studied under unsupervised learning, demonstration-based training, and unsupervised domain adaptation. It compares ways to combine demonstrations with reinforcement learning.

publication.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems

name: Synatra: Turning Indirect Knowledge into Direct Demonstrations for Digital Agents at Scale
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Synatra converts indirect procedural knowledge, including human-oriented tutorials, into direct demonstrations for digital agents. It trains a 7B CodeLlama on 100,000 synthesized demonstrations and evaluates the resulting policy on Mind2Web, MiniWoB++, and WebArena.

name: AppVLM: A Lightweight Vision Language Model for Online App Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: AppVLM first learns app actions from AndroidControl and then refines its policy through data collected in AndroidWorld. The study compares offline action prediction and online task completion for a lightweight vision-language smartphone agent.

name: How to Train Your LLM Web Agent: A Statistical Diagnosis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Studies compute allocation for web-agent post-training with teacher-generated supervised fine-tuning followed by on-policy reinforcement learning. It samples 1,370 training configurations and uses bootstrap analysis to examine hyperparameter sensitivity on WorkArena and MiniWoB++.

name: SEAgent: Self-Evolving Computer Use Agent with Autonomous Learning from Experience
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: SEAgent explores unfamiliar software using a world-state assessor and an automatically generated task curriculum. It learns from failed and successful interactions through adversarial imitation and GRPO, then combines specialist experience into a generalist agent evaluated on five OSWorld software environments.

name: CODA: Coordinating the Cerebrum and Cerebellum for a Dual-Brain Computer Use Agent with Decoupled Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: CODA combines a generalist planner with a specialist GUI executor and trains application-specific planners through decoupled GRPO. Successful specialist trajectories then support supervised training of a consolidated planner, evaluated across four ScienceBoard applications.

name: OmniActor: A Generalist GUI and Embodied Agent for 2D&3D Worlds
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces OmniActor, which shares shallow model layers while separating deeper parameters to train jointly on GUI and embodied interactions. A unified action representation and mixed training data support evaluation in both task families.

name: UIPro: Unleashing Superior Interaction Capability For GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: UIPro pretrains GUI understanding on 20.6 million tasks and then harmonizes interaction datasets through a unified action space. Continued fine-tuning uses the merged multi-platform data to train action prediction for generalist GUI operation.

name: Retrieval-augmented GUI Agents with Generative Guidelines
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: RAG-GUI trains a small guidance adapter to filter and summarize retrieved web tutorials while keeping the acting agent fixed. Supervised and rejection-sampling stages prepare the adapter for inference-time assistance, tested on offline web/mobile tasks and interactive Android tasks.

name: Scaling Synthetic Task Generation for Agents via Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: AutoPlay explores application states and functions to generate tasks, then uses a model executor and verifier to construct demonstrations. It produces 20,000 tasks across 20 Android apps and 10,000 tasks across 13 Ubuntu apps for supervised and reinforcement learning of UI agents.

name: BrowserAgent: Building Web Agents with Human-Inspired Web Browsing Actions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Trains BrowserAgent to use Playwright-based scrolling, clicking and typing directly on webpages for information-seeking tasks. Supervised and rejection fine-tuning are paired with explicit memory for conclusions carried across steps.

name: SynthAgent: Adapting Web Agents with Synthetic Supervision
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces SynthAgent, which generates tasks by exploring website elements and refines them when observations reveal conflicts. A later trajectory-refinement stage removes misaligned behavior before fine-tuning agents for the target websites.

name: WebSTAR: Scalable Data Synthesis for Computer Use Agents with Step-Level Filtering
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces a pipeline that filters individual steps from noisy computer-agent rollouts and augments them with reasoning for training. WebSTAR and WebSCORE support GUI-policy supervision and a distilled process reward model, StepRM.

name: UI-Voyager: A Self-Evolving GUI Agent Learning via Failed Experience
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces a two-stage mobile GUI learner that first co-evolves trajectories and policies through rejection fine-tuning. Group Relative Self-Distillation then uses successful rollout branches to provide step-level supervision for failed trajectories, evaluated on AndroidWorld.

name: MolmoWeb: Open Visual Web Agent and Open Data for the Open Web
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. The abstract states that artifacts will be released; this annotation does not independently verify release status or licenses.
summary: Presents MolmoWebMix, combining synthetic browser trajectories, human demonstrations and GUI perception data, and MolmoWeb screenshot-to-action policies trained from it. Browser benchmarks also test parallel rollouts with best-of-N selection.

name: EE-MCP: Self-Evolving MCP-GUI Agents via Automated Environment Generation and Experience Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: EE-MCP studies application-dependent mixtures of GUI actions and MCP calls using generated environments, trajectory collection and filtered training. An experience bank extracts rules from trajectory comparisons for inference-time improvement, distinct from model distillation.

name: WebAgentGuard: A Reasoning-Driven Guard Model for Detecting Prompt Injection Attacks in Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: WebAgentGuard separates prompt-injection detection from the operating web agent through a parallel multimodal guard. The guard is trained on synthetic visual/textual examples using reasoning-focused supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning.

name: OpenMobile: Building Open Mobile Agents with Task and Trajectory Synthesis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Presents OpenMobile, which builds exploration-based environment memory to synthesize task instructions and switches between learner and expert policies during trajectory collection. The resulting data includes recovery behavior and is tested through mobile-agent training and benchmark-overlap analysis.

name: AutoSurfer -- Teaching Web Agents through Comprehensive Surfing, Learning, and Modeling
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: AutoSurfer explores website actions breadth-first, retaining page and trajectory knowledge to guide task synthesis and trajectory refinement. It evaluates the resulting training data by fine-tuning a web agent on WebArena and examining synthesized-task diversity.

name: Mem-W: Latent Memory-Native GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Mem-W, which compresses previous trajectories and current-session segments into latent memory tokens used directly by the GUI policy. Self-distillation and outcome supervision train this memory representation for web and mobile navigation.

name: ToolCUA: Towards Optimal GUI-Tool Path Orchestration for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ToolCUA synthesizes interleaved GUI/tool trajectories and trains agents to choose between graphical actions and higher-level tools. Staged supervised and reinforcement learning culminate in online hybrid-environment training with a reward for efficient execution paths.

name: Weasel: Out-of-Domain Generalization for Web Agents via Importance-Diversity Data Selection
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Weasel selects web-agent training steps by balancing importance and diversity across states, sites and interaction patterns. It also prunes training accessibility trees around known action targets and regenerates rationales to match the model’s reasoning style.

name: AliyunConsoleAgent: Training Web Agents in Real-World Cloud Environments via Distillation and Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: AliyunConsoleAgent trains browser agents to verify documented procedures against changing cloud-console UIs through trajectory distillation and online GRPO. Provisioned rollout environments and backend audit-log checks support training and outcome evaluation.

name: Speculative Rollback Correction for Quality-Diverse Web Agent Imitation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Speculative Rollback Correction lets a student web agent execute short branches before teacher review localizes harmful deviations. Verified continuations and localized corrections feed supervised training while an archive retains diverse successful solutions.

name: ProCUA-SFT Technical Report
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ProCUA-SFT generates tasks and synthetic trajectories on live desktops seeded with document content, checking task preconditions before rollout. The resulting step-prefix examples are formatted to match inference context and used for supervised GUI-agent fine-tuning.

name: Trust the Right Teacher: Quality-Aware Self-Distillation for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Proposes quality-aware self-distillation for GUI coordinate generation under student-produced prefixes. A correctness-aware gate suppresses coordinate-token supervision that cannot reach the target box, while teacher-probability scaling adjusts the remaining signal strength.

name: Skill-Guided Continuation Distillation for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Skill-Guided Continuation Distillation first lets a policy reach its own off-trajectory states, then uses skill guidance to collect successful continuations. Mixing those continuations with expert traces supplies supervision for recovery states absent from demonstrations.

name: MemGUI-Agent: An End-to-End Long-Horizon Mobile GUI Agent with Proactive Context Management
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: MemGUI-Agent makes context management an action chosen by the same policy that controls the mobile UI. Structured history, UI-state and recent-step fields are trained from annotated trajectories to retain cross-app facts while limiting context growth.

name: WinDOM: Self-Family Distillation for Small-Model GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: WinDOM obtains bounding-box supervision from a Windows 11 web reimplementation driven through Playwright, and studies rejection-sampling distillation for small GUI grounders. It treats the depth of the supervised cold start as a GRPO choice, comparing same-size EMA and larger same-family teachers.

name: Empowering GUI Agents via Autonomous Experience Exploration and Hindsight Experience Utilization for Task Planning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: PEEU explores web environments and turns hindsight experience into aligned high-level planning supervision. A hierarchical task-decomposition analysis examines why atomic-skill competence alone does not ensure planning generalization across websites.

name: UI-MOPD: Multi-Platform On-Policy Distillation for Unified GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Uni-GUI, a collection of executable desktop and mobile trajectories, and UI-MOPD, which trains a shared policy from its own rollouts using platform-specific teachers. The distillation procedure routes each visited state to the appropriate teacher to preserve distinct interaction conventions.

name: MAGA: Multi-Platform Self-Fusion of GUI Agents via Structured Action Distillation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: MAGA distills specialized GUI agents into one policy by allocating supervision according to structured-action correctness rather than treating all response tokens equally. A training-only teacher hint supports fusion across mobile, web and desktop settings without changing student inputs.

name: Qwen-CUA: Native Computer Use for (almost) Everything
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Qwen-CUA operates through screenshots and keyboard/mouse events while compressing older visual history into reusable context blocks. Its report combines verifiable task generation, trajectory-based training and separate browser and Bash-augmented studies.

name: StepReflect: Structured UI Transition Reflection for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: StepReflect predicts structured per-action reflections from transition specifications and paired visual evidence. The paper distinguishes offline transition-label accuracy from online task success when the reflection model is integrated into mobile agents.

name: AppDeltaWorld: Transition-Grounded Delta Code World Model for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: AppDeltaWorld predicts executable code updates for the next mobile UI state, using transition-constrained retrieval and rendered visual assets. It evaluates reconstruction fidelity separately from policy training and adaptation using generated environments.

name: The Next Screenshot Knows: Gated Hindsight Distillation for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Gated Hindsight Distillation gives a teacher access to the next screenshot during training while the student sees only the available trajectory prefix. Distillation is applied when hindsight repairs a student failure, and the resulting policies are evaluated on Android tasks.

name: LookAgain: Closed-Loop GUI Grounding with Visually Grounded Reflection
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: LookAgain treats a GUI coordinate as a revisable hypothesis, rendering its marker and a local screenshot patch before confirmation. Reflective supervised trajectories provide a cold start, followed by GRPO using terminal grounding correctness.

name: ASIL: Replacing Screenshot-and-Click with Structured State and Semantic Actions
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.
summary: ASIL exposes application state as structured JSON and provides code-executable semantic actions. Its application benchmark compares this interface with screenshot control and application-native APIs, and studies supervised and reinforcement learning on the structured interface.

name: LLaDA-UI: Bringing Block-wise Diffusion to Vision-Language GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: LLaDA-UI adapts block-wise diffusion generation to a vision-language GUI agent through multimodal pretraining and GUI supervised fine-tuning. It evaluates grounding and navigation across multiple platform settings.

name: Towards Omni-dimensional GUI Agent Navigation with Masked Trajectory Prediction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: MaP unifies GUI-navigation objectives by masking and predicting components of multi-turn trajectories. Role-aware adapters address heterogeneous training data, and evaluations compare the approach with direct task-mixture training across navigation benchmarks.

name: Learn How to Act from Your Own Interactions: On-Policy Self-Distillation for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: GUI-SD-v2 extends on-policy self-distillation from grounding to multi-turn GUI interaction. It first strengthens responses to privileged guidance, then selectively distills step-specific reasoning and memory support for later actions.

name: Guides That Cause Actions: An Offline Study of Guide-Action Mutual Reinforcement in Multimodal Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: WebMRE pairs guidance sentences with grounded actions in an offline benchmark derived from successful WebArena traces. Controlled decoding-prefix interventions test how guide content affects action selection, while separating offline prediction metrics from live browser task success.

Original videos and extracted screenshots must be obtained separately; the code README explains that consumers download source videos from YouTube. A Windows Mobile unseen-OS test split is documented but is not labeled desktop Windows here. The companion code has an Apache-2.0 file, while the data card declares no data license and the repository defers third-party materials to original terms. Training scripts, pretrained checkpoints and the full generation pipeline remain planned updates.
summary: Video-derived mobile navigation annotations that pair scene boundaries and screen or element boxes with action labels for training and evaluating GUI agents.

name: Llama-3-8B-Web
notes: The ungated Hub manifest includes model.safetensors, pytorch_model.bin, config and tokenizer files; the two weight formats represent the same checkpoint and are not counted separately. The card describes an approximately 24K-example curated WebLINX training subset and evaluates dialogue-guided web navigation. Predictions still require parsing and execution in an external browser environment. The retained weight license is the Meta Llama 3 Community License Agreement, not WebLlama code MIT. No weights were downloaded, model used, or agreement accepted.
summary: A Llama 3 8B instruction-model checkpoint fine-tuned on WebLINX web interactions and dialogue, predicting browser actions from a textual state representation.
